newsitem.title: SLOVAKIA: SLOVAK TELECOM PLANS TO SIGN $100 MLN LOAN IN OCT.
newsitem.headline: SLOVAK TELECOM PLANS TO SIGN $100 MLN LOAN IN OCT.

text.p: The Slovak state-owned telecom monopoly Slovenske Telekomunikacie s.p. (ST) on Thursday said it expected to sign its planned $100 million syndicated loan with Citibank in October.
ST finance director Maria Rokusova told Reuters the revolving credit would have maturity of five years.

Earlier the official TASR new agency quoted the ST General Director Peter Valent as saying the loan would carry an interest rate of 6.5 percent and would be signed by the end of this year after the transformation of the ST into a 100 percent state joint-stock company is carried out.
"The number of the interest rate is not exact," Rakusova said, but declined to elaborate when asked to comment on Valent's statement.
"Also, the loan is not depending on the ST's transformation into the joint-stock company and we expect to sign the credit by the end of October," she said.
The loan is to finance part of ST's ambitious modernisation project, to be completed in 2000, of upgrading the Slovak telecom network to EU standards.
Overall investment into the project is expected to total around 55 billion crowns.
Transformation of ST into a joint-stock company is the first step towards partial privatisation, planned for 1998.
The move, however, requires changes to the current law on strategic companies, which are expected to be discussed at the parliament later this year.
By the end of September, British consultant N.M. Rothschild Investment Bank is to present a proposal on the optimum mode of entry of foreign capital for ST.
